I am currently pursuing my M.Tech in CSE Department from NIT Jaipur. In our 2nd Semester, Intel came to our college on 21 January 2026 for recruiting people for 10-12 Months Internship.

### Hiring Workflow :

1. Form Filling : Intel Workday Portal + College Google Form

2. Resume Shortlisting by different team(s)

3. Call(s) for Interview Scheduling

When you upload your resume on the Intel Portal, after a few days, different teams will call you individually to schedule the Interview (if your resume matches the team's expectations). I was lucky enough that my resume got shortlisted by multiple teams of Intel. They personally called me and scheduled the respective Interviews. In my case they called me on 29 January 2026 and scheduled the Interview on the very next day, i.e., Friday, 30 January 2026.

Interview started with my Introduction. Then they firstly deep dived my Resume Projects, firstly towards my ML Project which was a Regression Model. They told me to describe about this project, which model I have used, how data preprocessing is done, results, from where I collected the dataset etc. questions based on project and what mentioned in my resume. I tried my best to answer every questions asked. They have my resume infront of them. Then they asked about my second project i.e A Full Stack Web Application Project. They asked me questions such as why I used MongoDB as database and why not MySQL etc.

Leetcode at the beginning of 2020. It was a gradual grind till August, and I had completed around 330 problems by then. Here are some of the approaches and lessons I took away from the process:

* I followed a BFS-style strategy—starting with broad topics and the top 100 interview questions, then moving on to company-specific and topic-specific lists. Understanding problem-solving patterns is key.
* YouTube turned out to be a great resource. Channels like Back to Back SWE, Tushar Roy, and Pepcoding played a major role in simplifying concepts and problems that initially seemed tough.
